quest.title: Leroy: High Noon
quest.description: To fulfill your promise to Molli, you must get to the bottom of Benoit's story.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x200, Primogem x30, Mora x35000

dialogues.speaker: Door
dialogues.text: (We've already decided to investigate any strange goings-on regarding the Leroy family, knocking on the door would only alert them to what we're doing.)

dialogues.speaker: Door
dialogues.text: (Let's knock again once we have a better understanding of the situation.)

talks.objective: Go near Benoit's house to investigate

dialogues.speaker: Pip
dialogues.text: Hello? Anyone there? Do you still want your newspaper? Hey! Anybody there?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hello there.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is Benoit not at home?

dialogues.speaker: Pip
dialogues.text: How should I know? Either way, it's right weird, subscribing to a paper and not collecting it.

dialogues.speaker: Pip
dialogues.text: Whenever I delivered here, he would always at least reply, but recently, I haven't seen hide nor hair of him at all.

dialogues.speaker: Pip
dialogues.text: The copies of The Steambird I've left here are already piling up. You know him, do you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup, that's right. We're good friends of his.

dialogues.speaker: Pip
dialogues.text: Good friends? ...Eh, whatever. How about I give you the papers, and you pass them along when you see him?

choices.text: Sure. Leave them with us.

response.speaker: Pip
response.text: That's that, then. I did my best to deliver them. Don't you turn around and say I didn't! I've got other things to do.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That said, we haven't seen him recently either...

response.speaker: Pip
response.text: You too? Seriously, what's he been busy with recently? Could he have gone back to his old home? I haven't heard anything about that, though...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Old home?

response.speaker: Pip
response.text: That's right. His old place over in the Fleuve Cendre.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, so that's where he used to live!?

response.speaker: Pip
response.text: Wait. You didn't know that he moved here from down there? Are you really his friends?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... We...

response.speaker: Pip
response.text: Whatever, forget it. No need to explain. I don't care a whit what your relationship is.

response.speaker: Pip
response.text: Just get the newspapers to him, and I'll be grateful. Okay, here you go — I'm off.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm. It feels like there's a lot we don't understand about Benoit. Do you think this might have something to do with what we're investigating?

choices.text: It's probably related.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright then. Next up, let's check around his house a bit. Maybe we'll learn a bit more about him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That said, we can't make too much noise, or we'll alert that couple.

choices.text: The more info the better.
All yours, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Strange Boxes
dialogues.text: (You've seen these boxes near Benoit's house before. Judging by the traces left in the layer of dust covering them, they were opened quite recently.)

dialogues.speaker: Strange Boxes
dialogues.text: (Up close, a rank smell of fish and dampness assaults your nostrils, but when you passed by before, the boxes hadn't been moved. Where did the smell come from?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Urgh, this stinks like a sewer... This stuff didn't smell like this when we came around a few days back. Didn't Benoit say he only used these to store old furniture and stuff?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where'd this horrible stench come from, then? Did some new stuff get dumped here? ...Hmm, there's a piece of paper sticking out. Let's take a look!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This receipt's been torn up — only half of it is left. Huh, Bracari's General Store... We've seen that name somewhere, haven't we?

dialogues.speaker: Strange Traces
dialogues.text: (It has a slick, oily sensation that you're sure had to have been left by a candle.)

dialogues.speaker: Strange Traces
dialogues.text: (Who lingered here with a candle in hand, and for what purpose?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What can you tell me about this receipt...

dialogues.speaker: Bracari
dialogues.text: A recent sale of pliers, saws, and candles? Well now, that's a strange question...

dialogues.speaker: Bracari
dialogues.text: If you want ingredients for snacks, I've got them aplenty, but these things are difficult to move, darling, I haven't got many in stock.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We don't want to buy this stuff, Ma'am. We're just asking if someone else came to purchase them from you recently.

dialogues.speaker: Bracari
dialogues.text: Ooh, let me think, then... Yes, yes, I remember some people indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Bracari
dialogues.text: It was two youngsters, a man and a woman. They bought the items several days ago.

dialogues.speaker: Bracari
dialogues.text: They said that they wanted to do some woodwork at home, but needed some tools. Is something the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, no, no, w—we're just doing a... socioeconomic survey.

dialogues.speaker: Bracari
dialogues.text: A socioeconomic survey, you say? Hehe, you're here looking for information on them, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Bracari
dialogues.text: This happens all too often, little one. No need to try so hard to make excuses.

dialogues.speaker: Bracari
dialogues.text: The two of them went to Benoit Leroy's old house, if that's what you're asking.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could you tell me anything about Benoit?

dialogues.speaker: Bracari
dialogues.text: Ah, so that's what you're here for. Well, that's no surprise.

dialogues.speaker: Bracari
dialogues.text: Once you've reached a certain age, your past will catch up to you — it matters not where you move to.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you know anything about all this, Ma'am?

dialogues.speaker: Bracari
dialogues.text: Me? Well, I wasn't very close to Benoit. If you'd like to know about his family, you should look for Snodgrass.

dialogues.speaker: Bracari
dialogues.text: Go on, then. Snodgrass is a right layabout. You should be able to find him loitering about nearby.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could you tell me about Benoit Leroy?

dialogues.speaker: Areta
dialogues.text: Well, I've certainly heard the name, but he moved away a long time ago, and even before that, we rarely spoke.

dialogues.speaker: Areta
dialogues.text: I'm none too familiar with him, so it might be best if you asked someone else.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That box looks completely out of place, and it stinks...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I suspect it was brought here from the Fleuve Cendre.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Meaning that someone from Benoit's family went there recently... And he was from there himself, wasn't he...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #All the clues we've got have to do with that place, {NICKNAME}. We'll probably get more useful information there.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go, then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Off to the Fleuve Cendre!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What can you tell me about Benoit Leroy?

dialogues.speaker: Faustier
dialogues.text: The name's one I've heard, but I can't say I know him.

dialogues.speaker: Snodgrass
dialogues.text: Ugh, so boring... I don't wanna work... When am I gonna get rich...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me about Benoit Leroy...

dialogues.speaker: Snodgrass
dialogues.text: ...Leroy? Huh. I've heard that name before. Give me a moment...

dialogues.speaker: Snodgrass
dialogues.text: Right, I got it. Benoit Leroy owned a stall that sold all kinda stuff.

dialogues.speaker: Snodgrass
dialogues.text: Also, who are you? And why're you asking after this kinda stuff?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, we just...

choices.text: His situation's a bit complicated.

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: Uh... wait, um, has he done something wrong?

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: Oh, right, I getcha now... But, um, I gotta ask real quick, you guys from the Spina di Rosula, or the Maison Gardiennage?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You have the right to remain silent...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Anything you say can and will be used against you in a court of law...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #(Wow, you're really good at this, {NICKNAME}!)

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: Alright, alright! I get it. I won't ask no more questions. Well, not like he made an honest fortune or nothing, innit? Fontaine's got a lotta laws, he's probably broken quite a few!

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: Anyway, Officer, you've come to the right fella. Lemme tell you, I know all about Benoit, nobody knows him better — there's not much that scoundrel Benoit wouldn't stoop to.

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: Hmm. I'm old enough to get married, so he should be an old fogey by now, huh?

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: Anyway, I remember that his daughter, Autumn, was a real beauty — shame he never let any of us talk to her!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Autumn?

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: That's right, Autumn Leroy, his adopted daughter.

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: Just think about it. He was just a fella selling flotsam and jetsam, making a little Mora here and there — how'd he suddenly get rich enough to move up to the surface so fast, huh?

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: How else but by using his daughter, of course! Poor, pretty little thing — forced her to marry some rich old coot, he did!

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: And whaddaya know, that rich old fart kicked the bucket after just a few years, leaving his house to her. And what's hers is Benoit's — all in all, a pretty quick way to win a life "up there," if you catch my drift.

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: Tsk tsk, why did he get to be the one to get rich overnight— I mean, what an ol' bloodsucker, am I right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Wait, did something like that actually happen!?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Let's press him further.)

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: So, Officer, was that what you wanted to ask about?

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: I mean, if this stuff's useful to you, you could say that I've contributed to Fontaine's security, yeah?

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: And wouldn't you say that the Maison might wanna reward a... productive, upstanding citizen such as myself?

choices.text: We already knew all of what you just said.

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: Hey there, don't you worry, I've got other stories to tell. This is the Fleuve Cendre after all. I mean, how could a fellow lay his head to rest in peace down here without a few other peoples' secrets in his keeping?

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: Now, Autumn's second husband — oh yes, she remarried right quick, she did — lived a bit farther off, so we didn't hear from her for ages.

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: The next time we heard a peep from her... Well, she'd done... that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And what's "that"?

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: Wait, you don't know, Officer? She murdered her second husband. Got hauled off to the Fortress of Meropide for her trouble, too. You're investigating Benoit and you didn't even know that?

choices.text: Here's a list of the people involved in the case, Officer Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Ah, um, sorry, Captain {NICKNAME}. This won't happen again.

choices.text: Continue.

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: Right, right, I was just gettin' to that. Now, I heard this from someone else myself, but rumor has it that Autumn asked for her father to take the stand at her trial, but he refused.

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: Now, Benoit was unmarried, and she was his only kid... Right, and if I recall, even though she was adopted, her parents were related to him by blood.

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: Either way, since her one and only father didn't take the witness stand at her trial, naturally, she didn't have a chance. She was packed straight off to the Fortress.

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: Now, as to whether he did it just so he could take the house for himself or if he had some kinda disagreement with the girl, I'm not going to guess too much, hehe.

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: He usually puts on a friendly show, though, eh? I remember he always used to give out snacks — who woulda guessed that he was so cold-blooded?

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: Huh. Y'know, Officer, you haven't so much as frowned this whole time. Now, I thought I was a cold fish, but are you sure you don't have ice in your veins?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's a matter of professionalism.

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: And ain't that worth respect? Now then, Officers, what's the story with Benoit's crimes? How serious are they?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No comment.

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: Hah! That bad, huh? Well, what about his house? Will it be confiscated?

choices.text: Perhaps.

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: Hah, I knew it! Rats might scurry up to the surface, but a rat's still a rat.

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: Thanks, Officers, for making my day. I look forward to meeting you all again down here in the Fleuve Cendre. Hehe.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... This... Paimon's feeling a bit conflicted about this. Benoit made a really good impression at first...

choices.text: Don't judge a book by its cover.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Was Paimon just too foolish to see him for who he really was?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, this sure is a lot of food for thought. Paimon feels kinda queasy about it all — let's get out of the Fleuve Cendre as quick as we can!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's go, then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Time to get some sun on our skin.

choices.text: We've only heard one side of the tale from a random person.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, that's true, but Paimon doesn't think we can keep trusting Benoit like before...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, Paimon hates this feeling! Still, it's a good thing Paimon can always trust you.

choices.text: It is a distinct possibility.
And the secret you spoke of?
You didn't check the documents very carefully, I see. Very disappointing.
That will depend on what else you've got to share.

response.speaker: Snodgrass
response.text: Oh, I've got lots. I mean, this is the Fleuve Cendre. No one gets a good night's sleep around here without having a few other peoples' secrets in their keeping, hehe.

choices.text: We hope you'll cooperate with us.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: The Fleuve Cendre area just doesn't smell nice. It's not quite like "upstairs," where the air's the furthest thing from foul.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: How was it? Did you have fun strolling about the Fleuve Cendre? I'm sure you had a good time talking to Snodgrass.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y—You were following us?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How long have you been tailing us?

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: I have no interest in bandying words with children. *sigh* Even if you were to go home and tattle to your parents, I doubt they'd believe you.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: A word of advice — sometimes, what you see or hear is neither real nor true.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: When it comes to other people's affairs, don't insist on meddling until after you've got the full picture.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: By the way, Pip said that our newspapers are in your possession. I'd like you to return them, thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You have little choice but to give the newspapers to Athos.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: He gives you a cold look before swiftly turning and departing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's got a bad feeling about that guy...

choices.text: Ditto.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, this is so annoying! It feels like we've discovered something, but we can't put the pieces together.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And... and Paimon's kinda confused now. Benoit's a good person who's in danger, so we should be helping him... That's what's going on, right?

choices.text: We need to observe more carefully.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? Will that be okay?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, Paimon's assumptions have been overturned so many times these past few days that she's all outta brain juice!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But you sure are calm about all this — er, if Paimon was a bit on the stupid side, you wouldn't hold it against Paimon, would you?

choices.text: Of course I wouldn't, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, knew it! You really are the bestest, most reliable person in the world. Paimon's so lucky to have you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y'know, when you think about it like that, maybe Paimon's actually pretty smart! It's just that she didn't grasp the whole situation at first. Yeah, it's gotta be that!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well then, time for Paimon to put her brilliant little brain to work and figure out what we should do next... Hmm, have we, uh, accidentally alerted them that we're onto them?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If so, maybe we should just observe Benoit's house to see if there are any new developments, right?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's all we can do for now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alrighty then, let's return later.

choices.text: You're not stupid, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? Well, if even you say so, then it's gotta be true.

choices.text: Best to look before you leap.
Don't be too quick to judge.
Just what could they be planning...

dialogues.speaker: Door
dialogues.text: You hear nothing within the house. No one speaks, and you hear no footsteps either.

dialogues.speaker: Door
dialogues.text: It's a bit strange how silent Benoit's household is. Almost as if the place is empty.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: All we know is that Benoit Leroy used to live in the Fleuve Cendre, but we don't have a clue exactly where...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If only we had some clues to help us narrow things down...
